*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health
emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council
Meeting of May 18, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically
  for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the
  City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior
  to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the
  meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter.
  Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after
  8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public
  record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.
  2. By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the
  public can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the
  following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the
  conference 5 minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone
  line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone
  transmission. Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be
  inaudible due to feedback.
  l Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed below for the
  respective City Council Dates:
  ¡ May 4, 2021 – Access Code: 2012120# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 11, 2021 – Access Code: 2175831# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 18, 2021 – Access Code: 1813035# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 25, 2021 – Access Code: 2489941# wait two seconds and press # again

  3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable
  provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the
meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the
public access options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
   provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the
meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the
public access options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in
implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or
translation services in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable
modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-
412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall,
Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org
no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  May 18, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  May 18, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
  Powers Authority at the hour of 2:04 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
  personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item No. 3,
  an agreement with Bateman Community Living, LLC dba TRIO Community Meals.

127  APPOINTMEMNT OF MAYOR PRO TEMPORE FOR THE REMAINDER OF
  2021. It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that the
  City Council appoints Council Member Morales to serve as Mayor Pro Tempore for the
  remainder of 2021. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated May
  13, 2021, in the amount of $2,335,820.63 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on October 20,

  1
   May 18, 2021

  2020, October 22, 2020 (Special), and October 27, 2020 be approved. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21-162 APPROVED – BATEMAN COMMUNITY LIVING,
  LLC DBA TRIO COMMUNITY MEALS. Staff report dated May 18, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of an agreement with Bateman Community Living,
  LLC dba TRIO Community Meals for the provision of breakfast, lunch, and snacks for
  the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program
  (SFSP), per the 2nd Reissue Request for Proposals No. RFP-0157.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-162 in the amount of
  $304,243.25. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 21-103 APPROVED – AT&T/FIRSTNET. Staff report dated
  May 18, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a Participating Addendum and
  Pricing Schedule with AT&T/FirstNet to purchase air cards for the Police Department’s
  mobile data computers.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-103. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  REPAIRS ACCEPTED AS COMPLETE; PAYMENT OF INVOICES
  AUTHORIZED – CITY HALL EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER (EOC).
  Staff report dated May 18, 2021, was presented recommending acceptance of the City
  Hall Emergency Operations Center (EOC) parking garage roll-up gate repairs as
  complete.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Accept repairs as complete; and 2) Approve payment of
  invoices submitted by Lawrence Doors in the amount of $11,227. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 21-90 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET; PAYMENT AUTHORIZED - FOUR (4) INVOICES FROM BEST
  CONTRACTING. Staff report dated May 18, 2021, was presented recommending
  adoption of a resolution amending the 2020-2021 Annual Budget to provide funding for
  the re-roofing of the Main Library in the amount of $31,748.07.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 21-90 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE RE-ROOFING OF THE MAIN
  LIBRARY

  and 2) Approve payment of four (4) invoices from Best Contracting Services, Inc.in the
  total amount of $144,739.71. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   May 18, 2021

131.8  PUBLIC HEARINGS SET – CITIZEN PARTICIPATION FOR THE 2017-2021
  CONSOLIDATED PLAN. Staff report dated May 18, 2021, requesting that a public
  hearings be set for citizen participation in the 2017-2021 Consolidated Plan.

  Mayor Butts ordered the Amended Citizen Participation Plan for the 2017-2021
  Consolidated Plan received and filed.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set to receive public comments on the Draft
  Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Annual Action Plan on July 13, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.;
  and

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set to receive public comments on the Draft
  Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Consolidated Annual Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER)
  on December 7, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke against health and safety issues that’s occurring in her
  neighborhood, and problems calling in. She also requested Inglewood Police Department
  to address issues she’s having with drones.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke requesting an election schedule, and asked the Mayor to
  take care of his health.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Mayor Pro Tem appointed, specifically
  questioning the location of the appointment on the Agenda. She also requested for
  residents to be treated fairly.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Lenny Moore, nephew of Council Member Dotson, and Linda
  Tanniehill, Second Avenue Line Dancer at the hour of 2:28 p.m.

  Approved this 21st day of September, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
